items.heading: Neither Term Is Legally Defined
items.text: Neither term is legally defined or regulated the same way everywhere, so exact usage varies by provider. But across the wider career-services field, a genuine pattern shows up often enough to be useful.

items.heading: In Real Practice, the Two
items.text: In real practice, the two rarely stay in separate boxes. A counsellor who only hands you a decision and disappears has left the harder part, actually acting on it, completely unsupported. A coach who only pushes execution without ever revisiting whether the underlying goal is still right can end up driving someone hard in the wrong direction.

items.heading: Whichever Word a Provider Uses,
items.text: Whichever word a provider uses, these are the things worth checking before you commit.

items.heading: The More Useful Question Usually
items.text: The more useful question usually isn't "which label do I need", it's "am I still deciding, or am I trying to execute on a decision I've already made.".

items.heading: Paid Support, Whichever Label IT
items.text: Paid support, whichever label it carries, earns its cost once the decision gets expensive, time-pressured, or hard to reverse on your own.

items.heading: No Ethical Provider of Either
items.text: No ethical provider of either counselling or coaching can guarantee a job or a specific outcome, treat that claim as a warning sign under either label.
